name: [OPS] 01 · Route monitoring alerts
description: SKELETON — NOT A REAL EXPORT. This file lists the actions, names, types and links that /tines-build-story produces for the monitoring router (the Library 1231438 pattern: every production story's monitoring recipient), with placeholder GUIDs and formula sketches, in the exact agents[] order the links depend on. The first `/tines-export ops-error-router` (GET /api/v1/stories/{id}/export?randomize_urls=false&clear_recipients=true | scripts/normalize.jq) replaces this file entirely. Never hand-edit; links reference agents by index. Every key or type marked VERIFY is unconfirmed until read from a real export (docs/VERIFY.md #8, #9, #19, #23, #24); every payload path in normalize is written against the PLACEHOLDER samples/monitoring-payload.sample.json. Mode badge: none — a LIVE Webhook intake; it hands story-scoped alerts to [OPS] 10 through Send to Story.

diagram_notes.content:
**[OPS] 01 · Route monitoring alerts** — Mode badge: **Mode: none** (a LIVE Webhook intake; the Library 1231438 pattern).

Every production story names this story's webhook as its monitoring recipient (with the email DL beside it). The router receives failure and no-events notifications, tenant AI credit and event-limit alerts, team change-control webhooks and the pipeline's ship notifications; normalises them; dedupes per story + action + 15-minute window against the ops_alerts Record; enriches an action failure with its last level-4 log; classifies by a fixed rule table; delivers to Slack (a thread per story per day) or email, as the ops_routing Resource says; records the alert; and hands a story-scoped alert of severity >= medium (or a low one that repeats to the window threshold) to [OPS] 10 exactly once. It changes nothing, spends no AI credits and never posts a payload body. Unreadable payloads and delivery failures go to the ops_dead_letter Record.

Input: the monitoring notification body (shape VERIFY #9 — samples/monitoring-payload.sample.json) · Output: an ops_alerts row, one delivery, and the 16-field hand-off to [OPS] 10 · Failure: {status: error, error_category, retryable, message, failed_action, run_id} → dead letter.

Credentials by name: tines_api_readonly, slack_bot · Resources: ops_routing, ops_limits · Records: ops_alerts, ops_dead_letter.

agents.name: receive_alert
agents.description: SKELETON #0 — the single monitoring recipient (${OPS_ROUTER_URL}; the URL carries a secret, so it lives only in .env and GitHub environment secrets). Receives story-monitoring notifications, tenant AI credit and event-limit alerts, team change-control webhooks and scripts/ship_story.py notifications. Responds immediately with a static response — the sender never waits on this story (response option labels VERIFY). Watchdog: no events for 604800 s (7 days) pages the DL. path/secret assigned on import.

agents.name: normalize
agents.description: SKELETON #1 — one shape for every sender, DEFAULT() over the candidate paths in samples/monitoring-payload.sample.json `_normalize_reads` (every path VERIFY #9 until a real capture replaces the placeholder). Computes the 15-minute bucket, alert_id = <story_id>-<action_id>-<bucket> (the ops_alerts dedupe key), day, raw_keys (key names only, for the dead letter) and run_id. The CI fields come from scripts/ship_story.py's known body.

agents.name: classify_source
agents.description: SKELETON #2 — decides source (change_control | ai_credit_alert | event_limit_alert | story_monitoring | unrecognised) and kind (failure | no_events | credit | event_limit | change_control | unknown). DESIGN.md §3.6 names classify_source as a Trigger; a Trigger cannot choose among four branches, so the build makes it an Event Transform followed by one is_<source> Trigger per branch (AGENTS.md §4). The discriminating fields for every Tines-origin shape are VERIFY #9; the ship_story.py body is known.

payload.source: =IF(LOCAL.is_change, "change_control", IF(CONTAINS(LOCAL.text, "credit"), "ai_credit_alert", IF(CONTAINS(LOCAL.text, "event_limit"), "event_limit_alert", IF((CONTAINS(LOCAL.text, "fail") OR CONTAINS(LOCAL.text, "no_events")) AND normalize.story_name != "", "story_monitoring", "unrecognised"))))

agents.name: is_story_monitoring
agents.description: SKELETON #3 — a story's failure or no-events notification → dedupe.

agents.name: is_tenant_alert
agents.description: SKELETON #4 — an AI credit usage alert or an event-limit alert → dedupe (story_id 0 when tenant- or team-level).

agents.name: is_change_control
agents.description: SKELETON #5 — a team change-control webhook or a ship_story.py notification → the approvals channel only (never recorded, never handed off).

agents.name: is_unrecognised
agents.description: SKELETON #6 — a body classify_source cannot place → error (validation) → dead letter, with the key names only. Nothing is dropped silently.

agents.name: dedupe_lookup
agents.description: SKELETON #7 — Records action: search ops_alerts for alert_id == normalize.alert_id (story + action + 15-minute window). A Records check rather than the Event Transform's Deduplicate mode because the router needs the count and the thread (Deduplicate time gate VERIFY #19 if used instead). VERIFY the Records action export type and search/output shape.

agents.name: is_new_alert
agents.description: SKELETON #8 — no row for this window → a new alert: enrich, classify, deliver, record. VERIFY the Records action output path used in `path`.

agents.name: is_repeat_alert
agents.description: SKELETON #9 — a row exists for this window → count it; never re-post.

agents.name: increment_count
agents.description: SKELETON #10 — Records action: update the ops_alerts row — count + 1, last_seen; at RESOURCE.ops_limits.error_threshold_per_window a low row becomes medium and a persistent medium becomes high. VERIFY the Records update shape.

agents.name: reached_threshold
agents.description: SKELETON #11 — the new count EQUALS the threshold (fires once per window), the row started low (so it was never handed off), and the alert is story-scoped → shape_forward. All three rules must match (the Trigger's match-all option key VERIFY).

agents.name: is_action_failure
agents.description: SKELETON #12 — an action failure on a story → read that action's last level-4 log.

agents.name: is_not_action_failure
agents.description: SKELETON #13 — the complement of #12: no-events notifications and tenant alerts go straight to classify.

agents.name: enrich_logs
agents.description: SKELETON #14 — GET /api/v1/actions/{id}/logs?level=4&per_page=5 with tines_api_readonly (Viewer-role team key; read-only by role VERIFY #18). A 404 (the action was deleted since it notified) is EXCLUDED from log_error_on_status and is not a failure. Hardened: retry_on_status [429, 500-599], retries 5, emit_failure_event Always, failure path → error. VERIFY export keys for retries / emit_failure_event / log_error_on_status, and the response's list key.

agents.name: classify
agents.description: SKELETON #15 — the fixed severity rule table (README): 401/403 → auth/high · 429 → rate_limit/low · 5xx → upstream_5xx/medium · no events → silent_source/medium · credit alert → credit_burn/medium (high at >= 100 %) · event-limit alert → unknown/medium (high at >= 100 %) · anything else → unknown/medium. status from the notification, else the first 'HTTP nnn' in the newest log message (log message format VERIFY). excerpt = the newest log message with every secret pattern (LOCAL.patterns mirrors scripts/tines_common.py SECRET_PATTERNS, the same list as the monitor's scrub #79) replaced by [redacted] BEFORE it is truncated to <= 200 characters, plus its log id — never a body. Every Slack, email and forwarded use of the log text reads this scrubbed excerpt. VERIFY at build: the formula function names (REGEX_REPLACE, REDUCE) and regex flavour.

local.category: =IF(LOCAL.kind == "no_events", "silent_source", IF(LOCAL.kind == "credit", "credit_burn", IF(LOCAL.kind == "event_limit", "unknown", IF(LOCAL.status == 401 OR LOCAL.status == 403, "auth", IF(LOCAL.status == 429, "rate_limit", IF(LOCAL.status >= 500, "upstream_5xx", "unknown"))))))
local.severity: =IF(LOCAL.kind == "credit" OR LOCAL.kind == "event_limit", IF(normalize.pct >= 100, "high", "medium"), IF(LOCAL.status == 401 OR LOCAL.status == 403, "high", IF(LOCAL.status == 429, "low", "medium")))

owner_actions.auth: the story owner rotates or re-scopes the credential [BY HAND]; not a story change.
owner_actions.rate_limit: back off: pace or cache; a story change only if it persists.
owner_actions.upstream_5xx: escalate to the vendor; a longer retry is a story change.
owner_actions.silent_source: check the source system and its key; silent is not failing.
owner_actions.credit_burn: the costliest agent is named in the next sweep's credit check; at 100 % the platform stops the story.
owner_actions.unknown: read the log; the sweep triages.

agents.name: route
agents.description: SKELETON #16 — Slack or email, per the ops_routing Resource: the entry keyed by story id (set in the tenant after the first ship; the same key the sweep's dispatch_fix reads), else default. delivery = email only when the entry has an email and no channel. The email address is NOT emitted here — send_alert_email reads it from the Resource, so it never lands in an event or a Record.

agents.name: is_slack_route
agents.description: SKELETON #17 — deliver to Slack, a thread per story per day.

agents.name: is_email_route
agents.description: SKELETON #18 — deliver by email to the entry's distribution list.

agents.name: find_thread
agents.description: SKELETON #19 — Records action: search ops_alerts for this story_id and day with a non-empty thread_ts — the thread per story per day. VERIFY the Records action export type and filter shape.

agents.name: has_thread
agents.description: SKELETON #20 — today's thread for this story exists → reply in it.

agents.name: needs_thread
agents.description: SKELETON #21 — no thread yet today → this alert becomes the thread root.

agents.name: post_thread_root
agents.description: SKELETON #22 — the Slack send-message template (chat.postMessage) with credential slack_bot: the first alert of the day for this story IS the thread root. Slack answers HTTP 200 with ok:false on errors, so log_error_if marks that as a failure (key VERIFY). Hardened as #14.

payload.text: =CONCAT("*[OPS] alerts · ", normalize.story_name, " · ", normalize.day, "*\n[", UPCASE(classify.severity), "] ", classify.category, " on `", normalize.action_name, "` (", normalize.action_type, "): ", classify.owner_action, " Last error: ", classify.excerpt, " · alert ", normalize.alert_id)

agents.name: post_reply
agents.description: SKELETON #23 — the same template as #22, as a reply in today's thread (thread_ts from find_thread). Hardened as #22.

payload.text: =CONCAT("[", UPCASE(classify.severity), "] ", classify.category, " on `", normalize.action_name, "` (", normalize.action_type, "): ", classify.owner_action, " Last error: ", classify.excerpt, " · alert ", normalize.alert_id)

agents.name: send_alert_email
agents.description: SKELETON #24 — the Send Email action to the routing entry's distribution list (never a person). The address is read from the ops_routing Resource here and nowhere else. VERIFY the Send Email action's export type and option keys (docs/VERIFY.md #8).

options.subject: =CONCAT("[OPS] ", classify.severity, " ", normalize.story_name, " — ", classify.category)
options.body: =CONCAT("[", UPCASE(classify.severity), "] ", classify.category, " on ", normalize.action_name, " (", normalize.action_type, ") in ", normalize.story_name, ": ", classify.owner_action, "\nLast error: ", classify.excerpt, "\nAlert ", normalize.alert_id, " · ", normalize.occurred_at)

agents.name: write_alert
agents.description: SKELETON #25 — Records action: create the ops_alerts row (fields in ../ops-story-health-monitor/records/record-types.md). thread_ts from post_thread_root or find_thread, empty for email; channel = 'email' on the email route — never the address. VERIFY the Records action export type.

agents.name: should_forward
agents.description: SKELETON #26 — severity medium or above AND story-scoped (source story_monitoring, or story_id > 0) → hand off to the sweep. Tenant- and team-level alerts (story_id 0) and change-control notices never reach here. Both rules must match (match-all option key VERIFY).

agents.name: shape_forward
agents.description: SKELETON #27 — THE HAND-OFF SHAPE: exactly the sixteen fields [OPS] 10's receive_from_router expects (../ops-story-health-monitor/tests/sample-event.json), from the new-alert path (#15, #16, #25) or the threshold path (#7, #10) via DEFAULT(). A change here is a change to both stories.

agents.name: forward_to_sweep
agents.description: SKELETON #28 — Send to Story → [OPS] 10 · Monitor story health and credits (entry receive_from_router), payload = shape_forward, 30-second timeout (the sweep's send_to_story.timeout_seconds). The sweep's own kill_switch and lock decide what happens next; a busy sweep leaves the alert open for its next run. At most once per story + action + window. VERIFY the Send to Story export type, payload key and timeout key.

agents.name: post_change_control
agents.description: SKELETON #29 — the Slack send-message template with credential slack_bot, to RESOURCE.ops_routing._approvals.channel: a ship_story.py notification ('[env] change request <id> opened for <slug> at <sha7> — requires a named approver in Tines', with the source and run links) or a Tines change-control transition (field names VERIFY #9). Informational: approvals stay in Tines. Hardened as #22.

payload.text: =IF(normalize.origin == "ci", CONCAT("[", normalize.env, "] ", REPLACE(normalize.ci_event, "_", " "), " — change request ", normalize.change_request_id, " for ", normalize.slug, " at ", SLICE(normalize.sha, 0, 7), " — requires a named approver in Tines. Source: ", DEFAULT(normalize.source_url, "n/a"), " · run: ", DEFAULT(normalize.run_url, "n/a")), CONCAT("Change control on ", normalize.story_name, ": ", normalize.event_raw, " (change request ", normalize.change_request_id, ")"))

agents.name: error
agents.description: SKELETON #30 — every failure branch lands here: {status: error, error_category, retryable, message, failed_action, run_id}. validation for an unrecognised payload (message = the body's key names only, never values); otherwise from the failing action's status (401/403 auth · 429 rate_limit · 5xx upstream_5xx · else unknown); retryable only for rate_limit and upstream_5xx. Then dead_letter. VERIFY how failure-path links are represented in the export.

payload.message: =IF(LOCAL.invalid, CONCAT("unrecognised payload; keys: ", JOIN(normalize.raw_keys, ", ")), CONCAT("ops router ", normalize.run_id, " failed at ", LOCAL.failed_action, " with HTTP ", LOCAL.status, " — see the run's events"))

agents.name: dead_letter
agents.description: SKELETON #31 — Records action: the ops_dead_letter row with ref, error_class, status open, at, payload_ref (run guid + action name — NEVER the body), message (<= 300 characters). The DL still holds every raw notification, so a dead letter is a reference, not a loss.
